narrative_summary: The simulation forecasts a market dominated by risk aversion, characterized by widespread panic selling from retail investors and forced de-leveraging by institutions. Capital flows significantly towards safe-haven assets like gold and high-quality bonds, exacerbated by an oil supply shock, renewed inflation, and central bank tightening, leading to prolonged market fragility.
key_mechanisms: Retail investor panic selling and herding behavior.
Hedge fund and leveraged trader de-leveraging due to rising volatility and margin calls.
Mechanical rebalancing by pension funds and endowments when risk limits are breached.
Capital flight to traditional safe havens (gold, high-quality bonds, cash).
Strengthening of the US dollar as a global safe haven.
Oil supply shock causing re-accelerated inflation.
Central bank resuming monetary tightening, leading to rising long-term yields.
Deteriorating growth forecasts and widening corporate credit spreads.
Protracted risk aversion leading to slow re-entry into risk assets.
